title: Pentagon drops Anthropic; Danantara bets on Permian; Indonesia data-center safeguards
dek: A US defence blacklisting, a sovereign wealth fund's first overseas oil bet, and a civil-society push to regulate AI data centres each force a concrete decision this week.
summary: The Pentagon has stopped using Anthropic tools after a formal blacklisting, creating immediate enterprise-AI procurement risk across allied governments and forcing a reassessment of any defence-adjacent AI contract. Danantara has committed USD 250 million to US Permian Basin oil producer HighPeak, its first publicly confirmed overseas fossil-fuel equity investment, which sits in direct tension with Indonesia's stated energy-transition goals and raises governance questions about mandate scope. Indonesia's civil-society group IESR publicly endorsed a temporary halt to the BDx data centre at Jatiluhur and demanded green-data-centre regulations, a development that could delay up to 200 MW of planned digital infrastructure capacity. Black Hills Corporation's USD 1.8 billion power investment for a Google data centre illustrates the project-finance logic now governing AI infrastructure, where a regulated utility is taking long-term power-supply exposure. The Kementerian ESDM's study of real-time electricity tariff transparency, modelled on European practice, signals a structural shift in how Indonesian electricity pricing could work for large industrial and digital consumers.

signals.headline: Danantara invests USD 250 million in US Permian Basin oil producer HighPeak
signals.whatChanged: Danantara has committed approximately USD 250 million (Rp 4.4 trillion) to HighPeak, a US-listed oil and gas producer operating in the Permian Basin. Multiple sources including Tempo, ANTARA, and Kompas confirm the figure and the target company.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the danantara-bumn-karya-restructuring theme, now structural after 27 appearances. Danantara's mandate as stated by the Prabowo government is to deploy state capital toward high-return, strategically aligned investments. An equity stake in a Texas-based fossil-fuel producer is the first confirmed overseas hydrocarbon investment, and it sits in visible tension with Indonesia's JETP and energy-transition commitments. The investment also signals that Danantara is deploying capital at scale and speed, before its governance framework and five-year roadmap have been fully disclosed publicly.
signals.secondOrder: The Permian investment will be read by international climate-finance counterparts as a revealed preference: Danantara is prioritising yield over transition alignment, at least in this allocation. That reading may complicate Indonesia's ability to access concessional transition finance from multilateral development banks and from JETP partner governments, whose own domestic constituencies are tracking sovereign wealth fund fossil-fuel exposure. It also sets a precedent that Danantara's investable universe includes international upstream hydrocarbons, which will influence how future deal flow is sourced and evaluated.
signals.action: Assess Danantara's disclosed investment rationale (Kompas cites energy security and dollar-return arguments) against the JETP financing terms Indonesia has already accepted, and determine whether a written reconciliation of the two positions exists or needs to be prepared before the next JETP steering committee meeting.

signals.headline: IESR backs halt to BDx Jatiluhur data centre, demands green data-centre regulations
signals.whatChanged: IESR publicly endorsed a temporary suspension of the BDx data centre project at Jatiluhur and called on the Indonesian government to require that AMDAL documents, social and environmental assessments, and grid-reliability impact studies be released publicly before construction resumes. IESR also demanded that the government issue AI safeguard regulations and green data-centre standards.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the pln-grid-investment theme, structural since September. A credible civil-society energy research institute intervening on a specific project is qualitatively different from general advocacy: it names a project, cites grid-reliability risk to existing PLN customers, and sets a precondition for resumption. If the government responds, it creates a regulatory precedent that any large digital-infrastructure load must pass a grid-impact review before approval, which restructures the approval pathway for all future data-centre projects.
signals.secondOrder: The IESR intervention establishes that grid-reliability impact on retail customers is a legitimate blocking argument for industrial load additions, not merely an environmental concern. That argument, if accepted by regulators, gives PLN or Kementerian ESDM a procedural tool to sequence data-centre connections behind grid-reinforcement investment, effectively making data-centre timelines contingent on PLN's own capital programme. Developers pricing Indonesian data-centre projects should now include regulatory-delay risk as a base-case assumption, not a tail risk.
signals.action: Review any data-centre project pipeline in Indonesia for PLN grid-impact documentation. Where that documentation is absent or unpublished, assume a 6-to-12-month regulatory review risk and adjust financial models accordingly.

signals.headline: Pentagon blacklists Anthropic and stops using its AI tools, BBC reports
signals.whatChanged: The US Department of Defense has stopped using Anthropic AI tools following a formal blacklisting of the company, according to BBC reporting citing sources with knowledge of the decision. No official statement from the Pentagon or Anthropic has been published.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the enterprise-ai-data-privacy-contracts theme, which is now structural after 19 appearances since September. A defence-department blacklisting is categorically different from a contract non-renewal: it signals a security or compliance finding that, once documented, propagates automatically to allied procurement processes and to any contractor that relies on cleared facilities. Anthropic's commercial positioning as the safety-first frontier lab is directly contradicted by a national-security exclusion.
signals.secondOrder: The blacklisting creates a two-tier AI vendor market inside defence-adjacent industries. Firms that have embedded Anthropic APIs in workflows touching classified or export-controlled data now face a compliance audit obligation they did not have last week. Simultaneously, competing vendors such as OpenAI and Palantir, which have sustained Pentagon relationships, gain a structural advantage in enterprise bids where security clearance compatibility is a gate, not a differentiator.
signals.action: Any organisation with Anthropic deployments in regulated or defence-adjacent workflows should this week request a written compliance opinion on whether the Pentagon blacklisting triggers contractual representations or export-control obligations, and assess whether a vendor substitution clause needs to be exercised.

watchNext.item: Official Pentagon or Anthropic statement on the blacklisting: absence of a primary source confirmation means the BBC report remains single-source and the full legal basis is unknown.
Indonesian government response to IESR's demand for public AMDAL release on BDx Jatiluhur, and whether Kementerian ESDM issues a data-centre regulatory framework.
Danantara disclosure of HighPeak investment terms, including board approval documentation and any statement reconciling the investment with Indonesia's JETP commitments.
Kementerian ESDM consultation document or working group formation on real-time electricity tariff transparency.
Black Hills Corporation rate-case filing at its relevant public utility commission for the Google data-centre power investment, which will reveal cost-allocation and demand-commitment structure.
